sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: When you go to a concert, you might try to get there right when the doors open.
sentences.zh: 当你去听音乐会时，你可能会尽量在开场时准时赶到。

sentences.en: Or maybe you take your time and skip the opening act.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会慢条斯理，错过开场暖场表演。

sentences.en: But generally, you want to be there when the show starts.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，你希望在演出开始时人在现场。

sentences.en: In February, everyone who went to a concert in Haberstadt, Germany,
sentences.zh: 二月份，所有去德国哈尔伯施塔特听音乐会的人，

sentences.en: showed up 23 years late.
sentences.zh: 整整迟到了二十三年。

sentences.en: Alright.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Getting ready to head to the train station.
sentences.zh: 准备前往火车站。

sentences.en: One of those latecomers was Gabe Bullard.
sentences.zh: 其中一位迟到者是加布·布拉德。

sentences.en: Gabe's reporter living in Basel, Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 加布是一名住在瑞士巴塞尔的记者。

sentences.en: So he took the train a few hours into Germany to a pretty rural part of the country.
sentences.zh: 因此他坐了几个小时的火车进入德国，来到了一个相当乡村的地区。

sentences.en: Haberstadt is an old medieval town, like what you'd expect from a storybook.
sentences.zh: 哈尔伯施塔特是一座古老的中世纪小镇，就像你从童话书里期待的那样。

sentences.en: There are timber-framed houses packed close together, curving cobblestone streets.
sentences.zh: 那里有紧密相连的半木结构房屋，弯弯曲曲的鹅卵石街道。

sentences.en: But there wasn't time for sightseeing.
sentences.zh: 但没有时间观光。

sentences.en: The concert was well underway.
sentences.zh: 音乐会已经在进行了。

sentences.en: And Gabe was planning to leave early, because from this concert, everyone walks out early.
sentences.zh: 而且加布正打算提前离开，因为从这场音乐会开始，所有人都会提前退场。

sentences.en: It's a performance of a piece called Organ 2 ASLSP.
sentences.zh: 这是一场名为《管风琴2/ASLSP》的作品的演出。

sentences.en: ASLSP stands for As Slow As Possible, which is how the composer meant for it to be played.
sentences.zh: ASLSP代表“尽可能慢”，这也是作曲家原本希望它的演奏方式。

sentences.en: And that's how it is being played.
sentences.zh: 这也是它目前的演奏方式。

sentences.en: Very slowly.
sentences.zh: 非常慢。

sentences.en: And the reason I came all the way to Haberstadt now is because this was no ordinary day of the performance.
sentences.zh: 我之所以现在大老远来到哈尔伯施塔特，是因为这并不是普通的一天演出。

sentences.en: I came to see a chord change.
sentences.zh: 我是为了来看一次和弦转换。

sentences.en: The last time Organ 2 ASLSP had a chord change was 2022.
sentences.zh: 《管风琴2/ASLSP》上一次和弦转换是在2022年。

sentences.en: And this new chord will play until the next change, in August of 2026.
sentences.zh: 而这个新和弦将一直持续弹奏，直到下一次转换，也就是2026年8月。

sentences.en: There's a change the year after that, and the year after that, and so on.
sentences.zh: 那之后的第二年会有一次转换，再下一年又是一次，依此类推。

sentences.en: Until the year 2640.
The full performance is meant to last 639 years.
sentences.zh: 整场演出注定要持续639年。

sentences.en: The performance is in the church of a nun's cloister, founded in the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 演出地点在建于13世纪的一个修女修道院教堂里。

sentences.en: It's an old building, with bare stone walls, a floor that's mostly gravel, and a wood roof.
sentences.zh: 这是一栋老建筑，有着裸露的石墙，地面主要是砾石，还有木制屋顶。

sentences.en: When I went in, there were a few people looking at what I realized was the organ.
sentences.zh: 当我走进去时，有几个人正看着我意识到是管风琴的东西。

sentences.en: But it didn't look like a typical organ.
sentences.zh: 但它看起来不像传统的管风琴。

sentences.en: In the middle of the room here, there's a wooden structure with two kind of towers,
sentences.zh: 在房间的正中央，有一个木制结构，带有两座类似塔楼的东西，

sentences.en: and then some metal pipes coming out of it.
sentences.zh: 然后有一些金属管道从里面伸出来。

sentences.en: And they are making the sound.
sentences.zh: 它们正在发出声音。

sentences.en: Those pipes are making the sound that's filling this room.
sentences.zh: 那些管道正在发出充满这个房间的声音。

sentences.en: One sound.
sentences.zh: 一个声音。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: That's the performance.
sentences.zh: 这就是演出。

sentences.en: Well, at least until the chord change.
sentences.zh: 嗯，至少在和弦转换之前是这样。

sentences.en: At which point, the organ will play a different one sound.
sentences.zh: 到那个时候，管风琴将演奏另一个不同的声音。

sentences.en: Over the last 23 years, this tiny pipe organ playing this loud drone has drawn in thousands of fans.
sentences.zh: 在过去的23年里，这个演奏着响亮持续音的小型管风琴吸引了数千名粉丝。

sentences.en: Especially during chord changes.
sentences.zh: 特别是在和弦转换期间。

sentences.en: And as unassuming and discordant as it is, it tends to keep people drawn in once they hear it.
sentences.zh: 尽管它毫不起眼且充满不和谐音，但一旦人们听到它，往往就会被深深吸引。

sentences.en: There are people who come for every change, often traveling from thousands of miles away.
sentences.zh: 有些人每次转换都会来，经常从数千英里外赶来。

sentences.en: People who will stay in the church all day, just listening.
sentences.zh: 有人会在教堂里待上一整天，只是静静聆听。

sentences.en: People whom Organ 2 ASLSP literally brings to tears.
sentences.zh: 甚至有人被《管风琴2/ASLSP》感动得热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: I came to Halberstadt to find out why.
sentences.zh: 我来到哈尔伯施塔特就是为了找出原因。

sentences.en: As in, why does Organ 2 ASLSP even exist in the first place?
sentences.zh: 也就是，为什么《管风琴2/ASLSP》一开始会存在？

sentences.en: And what is it that so mesmerizes people about being in a cold, crumbling building, listening to this?
sentences.zh: 到底是什么让人们如此着迷于坐在一栋寒冷、斑驳的建筑里听这个？

sentences.en: The artist behind this very, very slow performance was John Cage.
sentences.zh: 这场非常非常慢的演出背后的艺术家是约翰·凯奇。

sentences.en: Cage was an American composer who started his career in the 1930s with well-received instrumental compositions like In a Landscape from 1948.
sentences.zh: 凯奇是一位美国作曲家，他在20世纪30年代开始其职业生涯，创作了诸如1948年《风景中的》这样广受好评的器乐作品。

sentences.en: Cage's compositions could be complex and modern, but they didn't always push boundaries.
sentences.zh: 凯奇的作品可以很复杂且具有现代感，但它们并不总是突破界限。

sentences.en: That changed in the 1950s, when he began experimenting not with the sound of music, but with the idea of music.
sentences.zh: 这种情况在20世纪50年代发生了变化，当时他开始试验的不是音乐的声音，而是音乐的概念。

sentences.en: His most famous piece is probably 4 minutes 33 seconds, during which the performer is supposed to sit silent for 4 minutes and 33 seconds,
sentences.zh: 他最著名的作品可能是《4分33秒》，在此期间，表演者应该保持沉默4分钟33秒，

sentences.en: while the audience listens to whatever sounds are in the room.
sentences.zh: 而观众则倾听房间里的任何声音。

sentences.en: The air conditioner humming, other people shuffling uncomfortably, the traffic passing by outside.
sentences.zh: 空调的嗡嗡声，其他人局促不安的挪动声，外面驶过的车流声。

sentences.en: I love the activity of sound.
sentences.zh: 我热爱声音的活动。

sentences.en: Here he is talking about it in 1991.
sentences.zh: 这是他在1991年谈论这件事。

sentences.en: If you listen to Beethoven or to Mozart, you see that they're always the same.
sentences.zh: 如果你听贝多芬或莫扎特，你会发现它们总是相同的。

sentences.en: But if you listen to traffic, you see it's always different.
sentences.zh: 但如果你听交通噪音，你会发现它总是不同的。

sentences.en: You can read all sorts of meaning into Cage's work.
sentences.zh: 你可以对凯奇的作品做出各种各样的意义解读。

sentences.en: Like, it's supposed to make us think about silence, or randomness.
sentences.zh: 比如，它应该是让我们思考寂静，或者随机性。

sentences.en: Or maybe it's not really supposed to make us think much at all.
sentences.zh: 或者也许它其实并不需要我们去过多思考。

sentences.en: In an interview, Cage quoted the philosopher Immanuel Kant.
sentences.zh: 在一次采访中，凯奇引用了哲学家伊曼纽尔·康德的话。

sentences.en: There are two things that don't have to mean anything.
sentences.zh: 有两件事是不需要有什么意义的。

sentences.en: One is music, and the other is laughter.
sentences.zh: 一个是音乐，另一个是笑声。

sentences.en: Don't have to mean anything, that is, in order to give us very deep pleasure.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，不需要有任何意义，就能给我们带来极深的快乐。

sentences.en: In 1985, Cage experimented with time and wrote the first iteration of ASLSP with the explicit instruction to try to play it as slowly as possible.
sentences.zh: 1985年，凯奇对时间进行了实验，写出了第一版的《ASLSP》，并明确指示要尽量慢地演奏它。

sentences.en: Here's one of the early attempts.
sentences.zh: 这是早期的尝试之一。

sentences.en: Now, if you're thinking that the letters ASLSP don't really correspond to the words as slow as possible, Cage is one step ahead of you.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你觉得字母ASLSP和“尽可能慢”这几个词完全对不上，那凯奇比你想得更超前。

sentences.en: The title is also a reference to a line in James Joyce's novel Finnegan's Wake.
sentences.zh: 这个标题也是对詹姆斯·乔伊斯的小说《芬尼根守灵记》中一行台词的引用。

sentences.en: The line is,
sentences.zh: 那句台词是，

sentences.en: Soft morning, city.
sentences.zh: 轻柔的早晨，城市。

sentences.en: Lisp.
sentences.zh: 口齿不清。

sentences.en: Where Lisp is just spelled L-S-P.
sentences.zh: 其中的Lisp只是拼写为L-S-P。

sentences.en: What that has to do with the music isn't really clear.
sentences.zh: 这与音乐有什么关系并不是真的很清楚。

sentences.en: But as more musicians began to take an interest in ASLSP, very soon, performers trying to follow Cage's instructions hit a wall.
sentences.zh: 但随着越来越多的音乐家开始对《ASLSP》产生兴趣，很快，试图遵循凯奇指令的表演者们就碰壁了。

sentences.en: Cage wrote this first iteration to be performed on piano.
sentences.zh: 凯奇写这一初版是为了在钢琴上演奏。

sentences.en: But there's a physical limit to how long a note can sound on a piano.
sentences.zh: 但钢琴上一个音符能发声的时间是有物理极限的。

sentences.en: You press a key, a hammer strikes a string, but the string will eventually stop vibrating.
sentences.zh: 你按下琴键，琴锤敲击琴弦，但琴弦最终会停止振动。

sentences.en: So the first performances of ASLSP lasted between 10 and 20 minutes, which is pretty long for a song.
sentences.zh: 所以《ASLSP》的早期演出持续了10到20分钟，对于一首歌来说这已经相当长了。

sentences.en: Just not, you know, long, long.
sentences.zh: 只是，你知道的，算不上长得没完没了。

sentences.en: Performers were stymied.
sentences.zh: 表演者们陷入了困境。

sentences.en: They wanted a way to play ASLSP slower, much slower, than was possible on a piano.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一种方法，能把《ASLSP》弹得比钢琴上可能实现的还要慢，慢得多。

sentences.en: But then, in 1987, Cage reworked the music for an instrument that didn't have any such limitations.
sentences.zh: 但随后，在1987年，凯奇为一种没有任何此类限制的乐器重新改编了这首音乐。

sentences.en: That's Klaus Ad Heinrich playing.
sentences.zh: 那是克劳斯·阿德·海因里希在演奏。

sentences.en: He's on the board of trustees for the project that brought Cage's ASLSP to Halberstadt.
sentences.zh: 他是将凯奇的《ASLSP》带到哈尔伯施塔特项目的信托董事会成员。

sentences.en: And he's director of music for the Halberstadt Cathedral, whose organ you're hearing.
sentences.zh: 他也是哈尔伯施塔特大教堂的音乐总监，你现在听到的就是他们大教堂的管风琴。

sentences.en: It's across town from the Cage project.
sentences.zh: 它在凯奇项目所在的城镇另一头。

sentences.en: And it's where I went to understand why the pipe organ is the perfect instrument for a performance that needs to last a very long time.
sentences.zh: 这就是我为了解为什么管风琴是需要持续很长时间的演出的完美乐器而去了的地方。

sentences.en: The cathedral's organ is on a big stone balcony that rises above the main floor.
sentences.zh: 大教堂的管风琴位于主楼上方的一个大石质阳台上。

sentences.en: To get there, we went through a wooden door and up twisting stone stairs with uneven grooves that have worn in over the centuries.
sentences.zh: 为了到达那里，我们穿过一门木门，顺着几个世纪以来磨损出不规则凹槽的螺旋石梯往上走。

sentences.en: At the top, Klaus Ad and I were in a stone area lit by the moonlight coming in from a gigantic, ornate window.
sentences.zh: 在顶部，克劳斯·阿德和我置身于一个石头空间里，月光从一扇巨大而华丽的窗户照进来。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: We're inside the organ here.
sentences.zh: 我们现在在管风琴内部了。

sentences.en: Impressive sight.
sentences.zh: 壮观的景象。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You can look down.
sentences.zh: 你可以往下看。

sentences.en: This was my first time being inside a working pipe organ.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次进入一个运作中的管风琴内部。

sentences.en: And my first thought was that the name organ fits.
sentences.zh: 我的第一个想法是，管风琴（organ）这个名字真的很贴切。

sentences.en: Like a bodily organ, a pipe organ is an intricate system.
sentences.zh: 就像身体的器官（organ）一样，管风琴是一个复杂的系统。

sentences.en: And this system is all about moving air.
sentences.zh: 而这个系统全靠移动空气运转。

sentences.en: And only air.
sentences.zh: 而且只有空气。

sentences.en: Which is also the reason an organ can play much, much longer notes than a piano.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么管风琴能奏出比钢琴长得多得多的音符的原因。

sentences.en: Its sound doesn't come from a vibrating string.
sentences.zh: 它的声音不是来自振动的琴弦。

sentences.en: It comes from airflow.
sentences.zh: 它来自气流。

sentences.en: The air is drawn from whatever space the organ happens to be in.
sentences.zh: 空气是从管风琴所在的任何空间中抽取进来的。

sentences.en: In this case, it came from inside the cathedral itself.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，它来自大教堂内部本身。

sentences.en: Klaus Erhardt showed me an opening with a screen over it.
sentences.zh: 克劳斯·埃哈特向我展示了一个带网罩的开口。

sentences.en: That's to prevent birds from going in and not coming out again.
sentences.zh: 那是为了防止鸟儿飞进去却再也出不来。

sentences.en: Sometimes they let them fall.
sentences.zh: 有时它们会掉下去。

sentences.en: And then they are inside and they die.
sentences.zh: 然后它们就在里面死掉了。

sentences.en: From the cathedral's interior, the air goes into the organ through the bellows.
sentences.zh: 从大教堂内部，空气通过风箱进入管风琴。

sentences.en: These are basically big pumps.
sentences.zh: 这些基本上是大水泵。

sentences.en: In the old days, bellows had to be manually pushed.
sentences.zh: 在过去，风箱必须手动推动。

sentences.en: Sometimes by people standing on them and working them like a big, medieval stairmaster.
sentences.zh: 有时人们站在上面操作，就像在使用一个中世纪的大型楼梯机。

sentences.en: But in modern organs like the one I was climbing around in, the process has been electrified.
sentences.zh: 但在像我正在攀爬的这种现代管风琴中，这个过程已经实现了电气化。

sentences.en: Klaus Erhardt went over to turn on a switch.
sentences.zh: 克劳斯·埃哈特过去打开了一个开关。

sentences.en: Now you see there's snow.
sentences.zh: 现在你看有雪了。

sentences.en: They're rising.
sentences.zh: 它们在上升。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: From the bellows, we passed through another door into a room full of pipes standing in orderly rows.
sentences.zh: 从风箱出来，我们穿过另一扇门，进入一个摆满整齐排列的音管的房间。

sentences.en: Then we went up a series of increasingly narrow ladders and stairs,
sentences.zh: 然后我们沿着一系列越来越窄的梯子和楼梯往上走，

sentences.en: climbing higher and higher into more rooms with more pipes.
sentences.zh: 越爬越高，进入更多有更多音管的房间。

sentences.en: Some were wider than a bowling ball, while others were barely bigger than a pencil.
sentences.zh: 有些比保龄球还宽，而另一些几乎比铅笔大不了多少。

sentences.en: The way the air from the bellows becomes music is by passing through these pipes.
sentences.zh: 来自风箱的空气变成音乐的方式，就是通过这些音管。

sentences.en: Every pipe is tuned to a note.
sentences.zh: 每个音管都调准到一个音符。

sentences.en: A, B-flat, C-sharp, and so on.
sentences.zh: A、降B、升C，等等。

sentences.en: But each pipe also has its own voice based on how it's made.
sentences.zh: 但每个音管也根据其制作方式拥有自己的音色。

sentences.en: It could be big and brassy, or thin and reedy.
sentences.zh: 它可以是宏亮铜管乐器的音色，也可以是纤细芦笛的音色。

sentences.en: An organist decides which voices to use by opening or closing what are called stops.
sentences.zh: 管风琴演奏者通过打开或关闭被称为“音栓”的装置来决定使用哪些音色。

sentences.en: If the stop for the big, brassy pipes is open, that's what the organ will sound like.
sentences.zh: 如果宏亮金属音管的音栓是打开的，管风琴听起来就会是那个样子。

sentences.en: And an organist doesn't need to choose only one stop.
sentences.zh: 而且管风琴演奏者不必只选择一个音栓。

sentences.en: Multiple stops can be open all at once.
sentences.zh: 多个音栓可以同时打开。

sentences.en: So a single press of a key sends air through multiple pipes.
sentences.zh: 因此，按一下琴键就会将空气通过多根音管送出。

sentences.en: This is where we get the phrase, pulling out all the stops.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们常说的“全力以赴（pulling out all the stops）”这个短语的由来。

sentences.en: I asked Klaus Ad if he could pull out all the stops for a single key.
sentences.zh: 我问克劳斯·阿德他是否可以为一个单独的琴键拉出所有的音栓。

sentences.en: Can you just walk me through one note as the stops open, and what the sound is?
sentences.zh: 你能否带我了解一下随着音栓打开的一个音符，以及声音是什么样的？

sentences.en: One stop after the other.
sentences.zh: 一个音栓接着另一个音栓。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Add each one.
sentences.zh: 把每个都加上。

sentences.en: For instance, we hear.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们听到的。

sentences.en: Also different.
sentences.zh: 也不同。

sentences.en: And so on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: And for instance, I can couple.
sentences.zh: 例如，我可以连奏。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊艳了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: As long as there's an open stop, a press key, and a flow of air, an organ can play a note like this indefinitely.
sentences.zh: 只要有一个打开的音栓、一个被按下的琴键以及气流，管风琴就可以无限期地演奏这样一个音符。

sentences.en: So back in 1987, when Cage rewrote ASLSP specifically for the organ, his instruction to play it as slow as possible took on a whole new meaning.
sentences.zh: 因此，早在1987年，当凯奇专门为管风琴重写《ASLSP》时，他关于尽可能慢地演奏的指令被赋予了全新的含义。

sentences.en: Cage died in 1992.
sentences.zh: 凯奇于1992年逝世。

sentences.en: But six years later, musicologists and philosophers met at a conference in Germany to determine what was the best way to play ASLSP really slowly on an organ.
sentences.zh: 但在六年之后，音乐学者和哲学家们在德国举行了一场会议，旨在确定在管风琴上尽可能缓慢地演奏《ASLSP》的最佳方式。

sentences.en: And how long could you possibly play it for?
sentences.zh: 而且这首曲子究竟可以演奏多久？

sentences.en: And they made something in Germany we called brainstorm.
sentences.zh: 他们在德国构思出了一个我们称之为头脑风暴的项目。

sentences.en: Reiner Neugebauer is the chair of the board of trustees for the John Cage Organ Project.
sentences.zh: 赖纳·诺伊格鲍尔是约翰·凯奇管风琴项目信托董事会的主席。

sentences.en: He says the conference attendees had some very different opinions, like whether the organist playing ASLSP could or should stay at the organ.
sentences.zh: 他说，与会者们有着截然不同的观点，比如演奏《ASLSP》的管风琴师是否能够或应该一直留在管风琴旁。

sentences.en: And one said, oh, the organist must go to the loo or eat something.
sentences.zh: 其中一人说，哦，管风琴师必须去洗手间或者吃点东西。

sentences.en: And then one religious or theologian people say, no, no, the organist must play until he fell dead from the seat.
sentences.zh: 然后一些宗教或神学人士说，不，不，管风琴师必须一直弹奏，直到他从座位上倒地身亡。

sentences.en: So it was a lifetime of the organiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是管风琴师的一生。

sentences.en: Reiner says these ideas weren't quite right.
sentences.zh: 赖纳表示，这些想法并不完全正确。

sentences.en: Because an organist can only play a piece for so long.
sentences.zh: 因为管风琴师只能演奏一首曲子一段时间。

sentences.en: But the music doesn't say a person has to be the one playing it.
sentences.zh: 但曲谱并没有规定必须由某一个人来弹奏。

sentences.en: You need not all the time an organiSt.
sentences.zh: 你并不需要时时刻刻都有一个管风琴师。

sentences.en: You can fix the keys.
sentences.zh: 你可以把琴键固定住。

sentences.en: In other words, you could find a way to keep the keys depressed so there's always a flow of air.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你可以想办法让琴键保持按下状态，这样就会有一股源源不断的风流。

sentences.en: No organist needed.
sentences.zh: 不需要管风琴师。

sentences.en: With this approach, the only theoretical limit would be the lifespan of the organ itself.
sentences.zh: 用这种方法，唯一的理论极限将是管风琴本身的寿命。

sentences.en: So when the organ breaks down, the music is over.
sentences.zh: 所以当管风琴损坏时，音乐也就结束了。

sentences.en: Out of this debate came an idea to play a very long rendition of Organ 2 ASLSP on an organ made specifically for the performance.
sentences.zh: 这场辩论产生了一个想法：在一台专门为这次演奏而制造的管风琴上，演奏超长版本的管风琴曲2号《ASLSP》。

sentences.en: The philosophers, theologians, and musicologists also needed a place to host this indefinite concert.
sentences.zh: 哲学家、神学家和音乐学者们还需要一个地方来举办这场无限期的音乐会。

sentences.en: And they landed on Halberstadt.
sentences.zh: 最终他们选中了哈尔伯施塔特。

sentences.en: Halberstadt was, in many ways, the perfect choice.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，哈尔伯施塔特都是最完美的挑选。

sentences.en: Because it might not seem like it, but in the world of pipe organs, this rural German town of 40,000 people is kind of a big deal.
sentences.zh: 因为你可能觉得不像，但在管风琴的世界里，这个拥有4万人口的德国乡村小镇可算是个了不起的大地方。

sentences.en: In restaurants and hotels, I kept seeing brochures that call Halberstadt Orgelstadt, Oregon City.
sentences.zh: 在餐馆和酒店里，我不断看到宣传册上把哈尔伯施塔特称为“管风琴之城”（Orgelstadt）。

sentences.en: On the back, there was a map to eight different pipe organs around town.
sentences.zh: 背面是一张地图，标注了镇上八台不同的管风琴。

sentences.en: That's roughly one pipe organ for every 5,000 people.
sentences.zh: 这大致相当于每5000人就拥有一台管风琴。

sentences.en: And the project's organizers knew about an old church in a nun's cloister called St. Bucardi that would be perfect for the performance.
sentences.zh: 该项目的组织者知道修女隐修院里有一座名为圣布卡迪的古老教堂，非常适合这场演出。

sentences.en: By 1998, the church wasn't in good shape.
sentences.zh: 到1998年时，这座教堂的状态已经很不好了。

sentences.en: It had been used for just about everything but religious services since the early 19th century.
sentences.zh: 自19世纪初以来，除了宗教仪式，它几乎什么都被用作过。

sentences.en: It was storage, a brewery, a barn for pigs.
sentences.zh: 它被用作仓库、酿酒厂、养猪的畜舍。

sentences.en: The city agreed to hand over the church to the project.
sentences.zh: 市政府同意将这座教堂移交给该项目。

sentences.en: But the performance was far from ready.
sentences.zh: 但演出远未准备就绪。

sentences.en: We had the location, and then we had to think about how long do we play.
sentences.zh: 我们有了场地，然后我们必须考虑我们要演奏多久。

sentences.en: Anneli Borgman is another member of the board of the CAGE project, along with Klaus Eerd and Heinrich.
sentences.zh: 安内利·博格曼是CAGE项目的另一位董事会成员，与克劳斯·埃尔德和海因里希同为董事。

sentences.en: And she says that figuring out how long to play isn't as easy as saying, play until the organ falls apart.
sentences.zh: 她说，弄清楚演奏多长时间并不像说“一直弹到管风琴散架为止”那么简单。

sentences.en: ASLSP is written as sheet music.
sentences.zh: 《ASLSP》是一首谱写好的乐谱。

sentences.en: It has a beginning and an end.
sentences.zh: 它有始有终。

sentences.en: You have to have some kind of tempo if you're actually going to play it.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的要演奏它，你就必须有一定的节奏。

sentences.en: So the foundation looked back into Halberstadt's history with organs.
sentences.zh: 因此，基金会回顾了哈尔伯施塔特的管风琴历史。

sentences.en: We have so many churches, and of course so many organs, and also organ history.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有如此多的教堂，当然还有那么多的管风琴，以及管风琴历史。

sentences.en: That history had begun in the 14th century with the installation of an organ in the town cathedral.
sentences.zh: 这段历史始于14世纪，当时在镇上的大教堂里安装了一台管风琴。

sentences.en: And so someone suggested, hey, exactly how long ago did the town's cathedral get its old organ?
sentences.zh: 于是有人提议，嘿，这座镇的大教堂安装旧管风琴究竟是多久以前的事了？

sentences.en: Let's play the piece for that long.
sentences.zh: 我们就把这首曲子演奏那么久吧。

sentences.en: Which came out to 639 years.
sentences.zh: 算下来正好是639年。

sentences.en: And so, on John Cage's birthday, September 5th, 2001,
sentences.zh: 因此，在约翰·凯奇的生日——2001年9月5日，

sentences.en: Reiner and the other members of the foundation gathered in St. Bucardi and began their 639-year journey.
sentences.zh: 赖纳和基金会的其他成员聚集在圣布卡迪，开始了他们为期639年的征程。

sentences.en: With a reSt.
sentences.zh: 伴随着一次休息。

sentences.en: At the beginning, there were just the bellows, because the piece starts with a break.
sentences.zh: 刚开始时，只有风箱在运作，因为乐曲是以休止开始的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so you just heard for the 17th month, just the bellows.
sentences.zh: 对，所以你刚才听到的前17个月，只有风箱的声音。

sentences.en: The bellows for the cage organ are in the back of the church, in a wood structure about the size of a small car.
sentences.zh: 凯奇管风琴的风箱位于教堂后方，在一个大约小型汽车大小的木质结构中。

sentences.en: They have a backup motor that keeps them going, and they haven't ever stopped pumping air.
sentences.zh: 它们有一个备用马达来保持运行，而且从未停止过泵气。

sentences.en: Even if that air doesn't go through any pipes and just vents out into the church.
sentences.zh: 即使这些空气没有穿过任何管道，只是排入教堂中。

sentences.en: After that first day, if you went to see the performance, that's what you'd hear.
sentences.zh: 在第一天之后，如果你去看演出，这就是你会听到的声音。

sentences.en: Just the sound of air moving through this contraption.
sentences.zh: 只有空气流过这个奇特装置的声音。

sentences.en: You could say this was the soft-morning city lisp, referenced in the piece's title.
sentences.zh: 你可以说这就是乐曲标题中提到的“轻柔的清晨城市嗫嚅”。

sentences.en: It was all very cagey.
sentences.zh: 这一切都非常符合凯奇的风格。

sentences.en: The organ's design was similarly notable for what's not there.
sentences.zh: 管风琴的设计同样因“缺少某些东西”而引人注目。

sentences.en: There's no piano-style keyboard or switches to open or close stops.
sentences.zh: 这里没有钢琴式的键盘，也没有用于开启或关闭音栓的开关。

sentences.en: The only controls are three small wooden keys on the front,
sentences.zh: 唯一的控制部件是正面的三个小型木制琴键，

sentences.en: with tiny sandbags holding them down to keep the air moving through the pipes,
sentences.zh: 上面压着微小的沙袋，以保持空气继续流过管子，

sentences.en: which sit in a spare wooden frame.
sentences.zh: 这些管子安放在一个简陋的木质框架中。

sentences.en: To make different notes, the foundation members replaced the pipes,
sentences.zh: 为了发出不同的音符，基金会成员们需要更换管子，

sentences.en: putting new ones into open slots and taking old ones out.
sentences.zh: 把新的管子放入空槽中，并把旧的管子拿出来。

sentences.en: Certain upcoming sections of the composition may require more pipes than the organ can currently fit.
sentences.zh: 作品接下来的某些部分可能需要比管风琴目前能容纳的更多的管子。

sentences.en: But because this is as slow as possible,
sentences.zh: 但由于这是一场尽可能缓慢的演奏，

sentences.en: Annalie Borgman says the question isn't urgent.
sentences.zh: 安内利·博格曼表示这个问题并不紧急。

sentences.en: This is the question of people after us,
sentences.zh: 这是我们身后的人要考虑的问题，

sentences.en: because the first part is ending in 2072.
sentences.zh: 因为第一部分将在2072年结束。

sentences.en: So I am 100 years old then.
sentences.zh: 所以我到那时就100岁了。

sentences.en: And I think they will, I don't know, perhaps in 2060,
sentences.zh: 我想他们会，我不知道，也许在2060年左右，

sentences.en: they will discuss how to go further on.
sentences.zh: 他们会讨论如何继续进行下去。

sentences.en: And it won't be the first time the piece has needed some adjustments.
sentences.zh: 而且这也不会是这首曲子第一次需要进行调整。

sentences.en: You might think that with only one note to play every couple of years,
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得，每隔好几年才弹奏一个音符，

sentences.en: what could possibly go wrong?
sentences.zh: 究竟能出什么岔子呢？

sentences.en: Well, it turns out, a lot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，岔子可多着呢。

sentences.en: The first chord change was on the wrong date.
sentences.zh: 第一次和弦变换的日期搞错了。

sentences.en: Early on, a reporter did some calculations
sentences.zh: 早期，一位记者做了一些计算，

sentences.en: and realized the project had gotten the math wrong.
sentences.zh: 并意识到该项目把数学算错了。

sentences.en: He told Reiner that the 17 months of Bellows blasting at the beginning
sentences.zh: 他告诉赖纳，如果这首曲子真的要持续到2640年，

sentences.en: should have been 28 months if the piece was to truly last until 2640.
sentences.zh: 开头那17个月的风箱轰鸣本该是28个月。

sentences.en: The slowest possible performance was moving too faSt.
sentences.zh: 这场史上最慢的演奏速度太快了。

sentences.en: The group postponed the next chord change to make up the time.
sentences.zh: 团队推迟了下一次的和弦变换来补回时间。

sentences.en: And now the piece is back on schedule.
sentences.zh: 现在这首曲子又回到了既定的时间表上。

sentences.en: But that wasn't the only problem when the project got going.
sentences.zh: 但当项目启动时，这并不是唯一的问题。

sentences.en: The first chord to play after the 17 months of rest was also too loud.
sentences.zh: 在17个月的休止之后，要弹奏的第一个和弦声音也太响了。

sentences.en: And it was a very disharmonic tone.
sentences.zh: 而且那是一个非常刺耳的不和谐音。

sentences.en: And it's, oh, what, what, what's, when you broke,
sentences.zh: 然后，哦，什么，什么，就像你坏了的时候，

sentences.en: oh, when the, when a car was broken, broken.
sentences.zh: 哦，当……当一辆车抛锚、抛锚的时候。

sentences.en: I said, yeah, yeah, so it sounded a little bit like this.
sentences.zh: 我说，对啊，对啊，所以听起来有点像这样。

sentences.en: And there was people who heard it and they go to the police and say,
sentences.zh: 当时有人听到后去报警说，

sentences.en: we can't sleep.
sentences.zh: 我们根本没法睡觉。

sentences.en: But you can't just turn a pipe organ down.
sentences.zh: 但你又不能把管风琴的音量调小。

sentences.en: The sound comes from air moving through pipes.
sentences.zh: 声音是由空气流过管子产生的。

sentences.en: There's no volume knob.
sentences.zh: 这里没有音量旋钮。

sentences.en: So for almost 10 years, they had to put the organ underneath an ugly plexiglass box,
sentences.zh: 所以在将近10年的时间里，他们不得不把管风琴罩在一个难看的有机玻璃箱子底下，

sentences.en: which warped the sound.
sentences.zh: 这扭曲了声音。

sentences.en: Then in 2011, they brought in two new bass pipes.
sentences.zh: 然后在2011年，他们引进了两根新的低音管。

sentences.en: The new pipes, plus some adjustments to the Bellows, made the organ quieter.
sentences.zh: 新管子加上对风箱的一些调整，使管风琴的声音变小了。

sentences.en: Two neighbors I spoke with, Jakim and Magit Troube,
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的两位邻居，雅金和玛吉·特鲁布，

sentences.en: say that today they can't hear the organ at all.
sentences.zh: 说他们如今根本听不到管风琴的声音了。

sentences.en: It's too quiet.
sentences.zh: 声音太轻了。

sentences.en: I asked what they think of it.
sentences.zh: 我问他们对此有何看法。

sentences.en: And Jakim said it doesn't really have a deep meaning to him.
sentences.zh: 雅金说，这对他来说并没有什么深层的意义。

sentences.en: You have to be an artist or a music lover to understand it, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，你必须是一个艺术家或音乐爱好者才能理解它。

sentences.en: Which, I guess, he was not.
sentences.zh: 我想，他大概不是这样的人。

sentences.en: But one thing Jakim does notice is that the organ brings in tourists.
sentences.zh: 不过雅金确实注意到的一件事是，管风琴带来了游客。

sentences.en: The project is good, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，这个项目挺好的。

sentences.en: The morning of the cord change, the cloisterous courtyard filled up a few hours before the big event.
sentences.zh: 在和弦变换的那个早晨，修隐院的庭院在大事件发生的几个小时前就挤满了人。

sentences.en: Uta Percy was sitting next to the church, sheltering from the wind.
sentences.zh: 乌塔·珀西坐在教堂旁边避风。

sentences.en: She had come from Hamburg.
sentences.zh: 她是特地从汉堡赶来的。

sentences.en: You're out in the cold, in the wind, waiting to get in?
sentences.zh: 你在寒风中在外面排队等着进去吗？

sentences.en: I've got my coffee here.
sentences.zh: 我这儿有咖啡呢。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: It seems pretty dedicated.
sentences.zh: 看来还挺有献身精神的。

sentences.en: I took a day of holidays.
sentences.zh: 我请了一天年假。

sentences.en: You're on vacation?
sentences.zh: 你在度假吗？

sentences.en: You took a holiday from work?
sentences.zh: 你从工作岗位上请假了？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Some people made even more of a trip out of the cord change,
sentences.zh: 有些人为了这次和弦变换进行了更长途的旅行，

sentences.en: even if they didn't know much about experimental music.
sentences.zh: 即使他们对实验音乐并不太了解。

sentences.en: Like Albert Schia and Peter Zee, who were on their first trip to Europe.
sentences.zh: 比如阿尔伯特·希亚和彼得·齐，他们这是第一次去欧洲旅行。

sentences.en: Well, I came here from Victoria, B.C.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是从英属哥伦比亚省维多利亚市来的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I'm from New York.
sentences.zh: 我来自纽约。

sentences.en: And you flew in just for this?
sentences.zh: 你们是专程坐飞机赶来看这个的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Kind of, yeah.
sentences.zh: 算是吧，对。

sentences.en: That's a good excuse to, you know, come to Europe.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这倒是个来欧洲的好借口。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the highlight.
sentences.zh: 对，这是重头戏。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the highlight.
sentences.zh: 对，这是重头戏。

sentences.en: Are you big Cage fans?
sentences.zh: 你们是凯奇的超级粉丝吗？

sentences.en: We have never heard anything.
sentences.zh: 我们从没听过任何作品。

sentences.en: About 500 people showed up, and as the change approached, the church doors opened.
sentences.zh: 大约有500人现身，随着变换时间的临近，教堂大门敞开了。

sentences.en: We packed inside the church, which was quite cold.
sentences.zh: 我们挤进教堂里面，里面相当冷。

sentences.en: Reiner and a few others walked in and gathered in front of the organ,
sentences.zh: 赖纳和其他几个人走了进来，聚集在管风琴前，

sentences.en: next to a music stand displaying the score,
sentences.zh: 紧挨着一个摆放着乐谱的乐谱架，

sentences.en: with lines marking each month of the performance.
sentences.zh: 乐谱上画着标记表演每个月的线条。

sentences.en: Another board member began to speak.
sentences.zh: 另一位董事会成员开始发言。

sentences.en: As the audience settled in, the speaker asked for a few minutes of silence.
sentences.zh: 当观众们安静下来时，发言者请求大家保持几分钟的沉默。

sentences.en: In the next five minutes, we will listen to the sound.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的五分钟里，我们将聆听声音。

sentences.en: Just relax.
sentences.zh: 放松就好。

sentences.en: It was eerie.
sentences.zh: 这感觉诡异极了。

sentences.en: I was surrounded by hundreds of people, no one making a sound, as we just listened to the
sentences.zh: 我被数百人包围着，没有人发出一点声音，我们就这样静静地听着

sentences.en: unchanging drone.
sentences.zh: 那永恒不变的嗡嗡声。

sentences.en: Then, wearing white gloves, Reiner approached the organ, carrying a new pipe, tuned to D-natural.
sentences.zh: 接着，戴着白手套的赖纳走向管风琴，手里拿着一根调准为自然D音的新管子。

sentences.en: As he lowered it into an opening in the organ, we could hear the air start to move, and the
sentences.zh: 当他把它放进管风琴的一个开口中时，我们能听到空气开始流动，

sentences.en: entire organ adjust to the change.
sentences.zh: 整个管风琴都在适应这一变化。

sentences.en: We stayed still for two more minutes, all of us surrounded by this new sound.
sentences.zh: 我们又静止不动了两分钟，所有人都被这种新声音所包围。
